title: Modbus Write Single Coil to Monitored Conpot Endpoint
purpose: Generate and validate one narrowly scoped Suricata alert rule for Modbus function-code-5 requests to the monitored Conpot endpoint without claiming that every write is malicious.

scope.in_scope_activity: Modbus Write Single Coil request using function code 5
out_of_scope_activity: claims of malicious intent based only on a write

evidence_selection.rule: Use development runs for generation and initial correction. Do not expose holdout runs to the LLM; use them only for final deterministic validation.

input_contract.integrity_requirement: Verify each finalized run manifest before its normalized evidence is used.

detection_behavior.plain_language: Alert on each Modbus function-code-5 request sent to 10.10.20.10 on TCP port 502, regardless of source IP, coil address, coil value, or unit ID.
detection_behavior.rationale: The baseline contains reads, while the controlled OT action and restoration use function code 5. Avoiding transaction-specific fields prevents overfitting to one rehearsed run.

candidate_rule_contract.title: Modbus Write Single Coil to Monitored Conpot Endpoint

deployment_target.activation: Install as an approved custom rule, run a configuration test, and reload only the relevant Suricata interface.

candidate_rule_contract.safety_boundary: The LLM may propose the rule but may not approve, deploy, reload Suricata, or modify pfSense.

expected_results.attack: At least one alert per attack run, with every observed function-code-5 request attributable to a packet reference. In the current write-and-restore workflow, the expected normal result is two alerts: one for the controlled write and one for restoration.
expected_results.baseline: Zero alerts across all baseline runs. Any baseline match requires investigation and blocks approval until explained.
expected_results.important_interpretation: The restoration alert is expected and is not a false positive; the network rule cannot distinguish authorized restoration from the controlled write.

required_checks: Validate Suricata rule syntax against the same engine and configuration intended for deployment.
Replay both development and holdout baseline PCAPs and record exact alert counts.
Replay both development and holdout attack PCAPs and record exact alert counts and packet references.
Confirm responses and function-code-1 reads do not alert.
Confirm the candidate does not restrict source IP, coil address, coil value, unit ID, transaction ID, or raw payload.
Record the candidate rule SHA-256 before approval and deployment.
validation.pass_condition: Suricata accepts the rule; all baseline runs produce zero alerts; all attack runs produce the expected function-code-5 alerts; every alert maps to an evidence packet; and semantic inspection finds no prohibited restriction.
validation.reporting_boundary: PASS applies only to this lab dataset and does not establish accuracy, false-positive rate, or general OT coverage.

benign_lookalikes: Authorized maintenance using Write Single Coil
Legitimate commissioning or testing against the monitored endpoint
limitations: The rule identifies a control write, not attacker identity or intent.
Legitimate function-code-5 writes to the monitored endpoint will alert.
The rule cannot distinguish the controlled write from restoration.
A reads-only baseline is too limited for false-positive-rate or accuracy claims.
The rule covers one monitored Conpot endpoint and does not generalize to other OT assets or protocols.
Detection depends on the pfSense capture point seeing the request and Suricata parsing Modbus traffic.
remaining_predeployment_facts: Record the Suricata engine and pfSense package versions.
Confirm the Modbus app-layer parser is enabled on the deployment interface.
Record the active Suricata configuration hash and approved candidate rule hash.

material_changes: Replaced stale pending-evidence gates with the completed-run development and holdout workflow.
Named modbus_requests.jsonl and its exact nested fields as the LLM input contract.
Added the required Suricata artifact type and concrete pfSense deployment target.
Defined expected attack and baseline results without treating expected values as observed results.
Reduced optional synthetic testing and retained only checks needed to validate the MVP safely.
blackbox_review.nonblocking_note: Populate the listed Suricata environment facts during validation/deployment; do not spend additional specification time on them now.
